**Image Analysis:**

- A banana plant with a bunch of green fruit (bananas) in the center
- The large leaf in the foreground shows pronounced browning/yellowing at the margins and tips
- Older leaves appear to be wilting and hanging/drooping around the pseudostem
- The green banana bunch appears relatively normal with no obvious fruit symptoms
- Overall plant shows stress with leaf deterioration progressing on older foliage

**Reasoning against other classes:**
- No distinct black/dark streaks or spots on leaf surfaces → rules out Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka
- No oval/circular lesions on leaves → rules out Cordana_Leaf_Spot
- No dark rot at fruit tips → rules out Cigar_End_Rot
- No bunching of narrow upright leaves → rules out Bunchy_Top
- No visible dark lesions/anthracnose spots → rules out Anthracnose

**Match to Panama Disease:**
- Yellowing and wilting of older leaves is evident, consistent with the description of yellowing progressing from older to younger leaves
- Leaves appear to collapse/hang around the pseudostem ("like a skirt")
- The banana fruit shows no specific disease symptoms — matching the description exactly ("Fruit does not show any specific disease symptoms")
- The overall plant wilting pattern fits vascular wilt etiology
